South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 78 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 03/14/26 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for COPD management, evaluation of persistent bilateral lower extremity edema, and assessment of fatigue and psychological well-being.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for a follow-up visit, primarily to address his ongoing management of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), persistent bilateral lower extremity edema, and fatigue. He reports that while he has continued to use the albuterol inhaler six times daily, he is still experiencing significant dyspnea, particularly with exertion. He notes that cold weather exacerbates his symptoms, leading to increased reliance on his bronchodilator.
The bilateral lower extremity edema has shown minimal improvement despite adherence to dietary sodium restrictions and continued furosemide therapy, which remains at 80 mg daily. The edema is still characterized as 1+ pitting, particularly noticeable after prolonged sitting, and he continues to deny any associated pain or erythema. He expresses concern that the edema affects his mobility and overall quality of life.
Mr. Fairfax reports that his fatigue persists and remains debilitating, significantly affecting his ability to partake in social activities and complete daily tasks. He also notes persistent feelings of anxiety and low mood, with increased frequency of depressive episodes, which he attributes to his ongoing health struggles.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + persistent fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + daytime dyspnea, + nocturnal wheezing, - cough, - sputum production, no hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain in knees and hands, no swelling. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis 4. Persistent fatigue 5. Anxiety and depression (ongoing management)
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed, continued use at six times daily. 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily. 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 MDI, 1 puff twice daily. 4. Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaler, 1 puff daily. 5. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain. 6. Furosemide 80 mg daily. 7. Sertraline 50 mg daily (ongoing management for anxiety and depression).
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.7F, HR 80, BP 128/82, RR 24, O2 sat 88% on room air
General: Elderly male in no acute distress but appears fatigued and anxious. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, moderate wheezing noted on expiration, no crackles. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 1+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 8.6, Hgb 11.5, Hct 34.5, Plt 210 2. BMP: Na 135, K 4.1, Cl 95, CO2 25, BUN 20, Cr 1.3, Glucose 90 3. BNP: 495 (stable). 4. Thyroid function tests: TSH 3.5 (within normal limits).
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: The patient continues to experience significant dyspnea despite ongoing therapy. Maintain the current regimen of tiotropium and fluticasone/salmeterol. A referral to pulmonary rehabilitation is recommended to improve exercise tolerance and overall quality of life. Follow-up in 1 month for reassessment. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. Blood pressure remains stable. Follow-up in 1 month. 3. Lower extremity edema: The edema persists. Reinforce dietary sodium restrictions and encourage Mr. Fairfax to elevate his legs more frequently. A referral to nephrology will be arranged if no improvement is noted by the next follow-up. 4. Fatigue and psychological well-being: Given the ongoing symptoms of fatigue and anxiety/depression, continue sertraline 50 mg daily. Schedule follow-up with a psychologist for ongoing support. Monitor CBC and metabolic panel in one month to assess for any changes.
Patient education reiterated regarding recognizing signs of exacerbation, adherence to medication, and lifestyle modifications to effectively manage COPD and edema.
